# Diogo Fitness

> Diogo Fitness (Diogo Fit) is one-to-one online fitness coaching from Diogo Camera, based in South Florida, for clients anywhere in the world.

Coaching is online and sold only through a conversation: there are no prices on this site. Apply at https://diogofit.com/apply/.

## Pages

### Diogo Camera, Online Fitness Coach
URL: https://diogofit.com/about/
Diogo Camera is an online fitness coach based in South Florida. He used to build his days around comfort. Now he helps people build theirs around structure.

### Apply for Online Coaching
URL: https://diogofit.com/apply/
Apply for online fitness coaching with Diogo: answer a few short questions and send him the message on Instagram, or use the full application form.

### How to Stop Starting Over With Fitness

Starting over usually isn't a willpower problem. It's a system problem: decide ahead, shrink the plan for bad weeks, never miss twice, have a witness.
Short answer: If you keep starting over, it usually isn't a willpower problem. It's a system problem: decide ahead of time, shrink the plan for bad weeks, never miss twice and have a witness who sees your numbers.

### What Is Online Fitness Coaching? How It Works
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/what-is-online-fitness-coaching/
Online coaching is a personalized training plan on your phone, with practical nutrition guidance and a real coach checking in weekly. How it works and who it's for.
Short answer: Online fitness coaching is a service where a real coach builds your training plan and nutrition guidance, you follow it in an app, and the coach reviews your numbers and adjusts the plan on a set schedule, all from a distance. It fits people who can get to a place to train but struggle to stay consistent.

### How to Stay Consistent With Working Out
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/consistency-vs-motivation/
Motivation comes and goes, so plan for the days you don't feel like it: set days and times, a smaller workout on bad days, and never miss twice.
Short answer: Motivation comes and goes, so don't build your training on it. Plan for the days you don't feel like it: pick set days and times, have a smaller workout for bad days, and never miss twice in a row.

For most people: strength usually improves first, measurable muscle around weeks 4 to 8, and visible fat loss often takes 8 to 12 weeks or more.

Short answer: The 80/20 approach means most of what you eat is filling, protein-rich, mostly unprocessed food, and the rest is food you simply enjoy. It's a guideline, not a rule: calories and protein still count.

### RIR Meaning: Reps in Reserve and How to Use It

Short answer: Reps in reserve (RIR) is how many more good reps you could have done before failure. For most working sets, aim for about 1 to 3 reps in reserve.

### How to Get Back Into the Gym After a Long Break
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/getting-back-into-training/
After months off you keep more than you think, mostly strength. Start lighter than your old numbers, train two or three times a week and build back over six weeks.
Short answer: After a long break you keep more than you think, especially strength. How far back you start depends on how long you were away; after a long one, start at about half your old volume with weights that feel easy, train two or three times a week, and build back over the next six weeks.

### Online Coaching vs Personal Trainer: Side by Side

Short answer: Choose a personal trainer if you want someone beside you to correct your form during scheduled sessions. Choose an online coach if you can train on your own but need a plan, check-ins and structure for the whole week.

### Gym Anxiety? How to Get Through Your First Day

### How to Start Lifting Weights: First 4 Weeks
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/how-to-start-lifting-weights/
How to start lifting weights as a beginner: six movements, two or three short sessions a week, weights that feel too easy, and exactly when to add more.
Short answer: Start with two or three full-body sessions a week built from six movements: a squat, a hinge, a push, a pull, a carry or core move, and a machine you like. Two sets each, three or four reps in reserve, and add a little when the top of the range feels easy.

### Dumbbell Workout Plan: 3 Days a Week at Home
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/dumbbell-workout-plan/
A three-day dumbbell workout plan for home: six movements a session, two to three sets, weights that feel too easy, and a four-week rule for adding more.
Short answer: Three full-body sessions a week, forty minutes each, six dumbbell movements per session: a squat, a hinge, a push, a pull, a shoulder move and a core move. Two to three sets of eight to twelve reps, stopping with three or four reps left, and add a little every week the top of the range feels easy.

### Full-Body Workout Plan: 3 Days a Week
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/full-body-workout-plan/
A free 3-day full-body workout plan for the gym: three sessions of six movements, the sets, reps and rest, an eight-week progression rule, and a printable PDF.
Short answer: Three full-body gym sessions a week, about an hour each, six movements per session: a squat, a hinge, a push, a pull, one extra and a core move. Three sets of eight to twelve, stopping two or three reps short of failure, resting about two minutes on the big lifts. Add weight whenever you hit twelve on every set.

### College Workout Routine: A 3-Day Semester Plan
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/college-workout-routine/
A college workout routine built around your classes: three full-body sessions a week, a two-day version for exam weeks, and a plan for the whole semester.
Short answer: Lift three days a week, with a day between sessions, around your class schedule: six full-body movements, two to three sets of eight to twelve reps, stopping each set with two or three reps left. In exam weeks, drop to two shorter sessions and hold your weights. Add a little whenever the top of the rep range feels easy.

### PPL vs Full Body vs Upper/Lower: Which Split?
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/workout-split/
PPL vs full body? With weekly sets matched, studies find similar gains. Pick the split for your days: full body for 2 or 3, upper/lower for 4, PPL for 5 or 6.
Short answer: Count the days you can train, then pick the split that fits them: full body for two or three days, upper/lower for four, push/pull/legs for five or six. When weekly volume is matched, studies find split and full-body routines build similar strength and muscle, so choose the one you'll repeat and count your sets.

### Upper/Lower Split Workout Plan: 4 Days a Week
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/upper-lower-split-workout-plan/
A free 4-day upper/lower split workout plan: two upper and two lower sessions with sets and reps, how to count weekly sets, progression and a printable PDF.
Short answer: Four sessions a week, two upper body and two lower body, so every muscle is trained twice. Six exercises a session: three sets of five to eight on the big lifts, eight to fifteen on the rest, stopping two or three reps short of failure. Add weight whenever you hit the top of the range on every set.

### How Many Rest Days a Week Do You Need?
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/rest-days/
How many rest days a week you need, whether it's bad to work out every day, what a rest or active recovery day looks like, and how rest fits a 3- or 4-day plan.
Short answer: Lifting two to four days a week leaves three to five rest days, and that's enough for most people. What matters more is a day between hard sessions for the same muscles. Training every day isn't required: with the same weekly work, six days a week built about the same strength and muscle as three.

### 30-Minute Full-Body Workout for the Gym or Home
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/30-minute-workout/
A 30-minute full-body workout for the gym or home: a short warm-up, a squat, then two pairs. When 30 minutes is enough, what to cut first, and how to progress.
Short answer: Thirty minutes is enough for a full-body session built around the big movements: warm-up sets of the squat, the squat itself, then a push paired with a pull and a hinge paired with a core move. Two or three times a week; add a rep or a little weight when the top of the range gets easy.

### Push/Pull/Legs Routine: 6-Day and 3-Day Plans
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/push-pull-legs-routine/
A free push/pull/legs routine: two push, two pull and two leg sessions with sets and reps, the 6-day week, the 3-day version, progression and a printable PDF.
Short answer: Push (chest, shoulders, triceps), pull (back, biceps) and legs, each run twice a week with one day off, so every muscle is trained twice. Five or six exercises a session: three sets of five to eight on the first lift, eight to fifteen on the rest, two or three reps short of failure. On three days, run each session once.

### Best Time to Work Out: Morning or Night?
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/best-time-to-work-out/
The best time to work out is the one you can repeat. What research says about morning vs evening lifting, how to pick your slot, and early-morning tips.
Short answer: The best time to work out is the one you can repeat. Morning and evening lifting build about the same strength and muscle, even though most are a little stronger later. Pick a slot your week protects, keep it, and if it's early, warm up with lighter sets of your first lift.

### Deload Week: What It Is and When to Take One
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/deload-week/
A deload week is a planned lighter week of lifting. What it is, how often lifters take one, how to cut sets or weight, and how it differs from a week off.
Short answer: A deload week is a planned lighter week: the same days and exercises, with fewer sets, lighter weights or sets stopped further from failure. Coaches commonly program one every four to six weeks, but that's practice, not proof: the research on deloading is still limited. Take one when it's planned or when progress stalls.

### How Active Is Your Metro? CDC Data, 48 Metros
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/how-active-is-your-metro/
48 large U.S. metros in one table: adults reporting no physical activity in the past month and adults lifting twice a week, from the CDC's metro-area survey.
Short answer: In the CDC's metro-area survey, the share of adults reporting no physical activity in the past month runs from 14.4% to 29.1% across the 40 of these 48 metros with a 2023 or 2024 figure, and the share doing muscle-strengthening exercises twice a week from 35.3% to 46.7% (2023). Eight of the 48 have no recent CDC figure.
Data (CSV): https://diogofit.com/learn/how-active-is-your-metro/how-active-is-your-metro.csv

### How to Warm Up Before Lifting: Warm-Up Sets
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/how-to-warm-up-before-lifting/
How to warm up before lifting: easy movement, then warm-up sets of your first lift. How many sets, at what weights, and dynamic vs static stretching.
Short answer: Spend a few minutes moving easily, then do two to four warm-up sets of your first lift, climbing from about half your working weight to about 80% of it, with fewer reps each time. Later exercises for the same muscles need one light set or none. Keep long static stretches for after the session.

### Summer Heat by Metro: 90-Degree Days, July Highs
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/summer-heat-by-metro/
NOAA's 1991–2020 normals at weather stations in 48 big U.S. metros: days a year at or above 90 F, the average July high, and when to move outdoor training.
Short answer: NOAA's 1991–2020 normals put the days a year at or above 90 F between 2.1 (Seattle) and 173.4 (Phoenix) at principal-city weather stations in 46 large U.S. metros. Where the count is high, move hard outdoor work to the early morning or evening in those months and keep lifting indoors exactly as planned.
Data (CSV): https://diogofit.com/learn/summer-heat-by-metro/summer-heat-by-metro.csv

### Cardio Before or After Weights? Order and Timing
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/cardio-and-lifting/
Cardio before or after weights? Lift first if strength is the goal. Same day or separate days, how big the interference effect is, how much cardio, which kind.
Short answer: Lift first, then do cardio, if strength is your priority: in studies, that order built more lower-body strength than the reverse. For most people, adding cardio doesn't cost muscle size or maximal strength, on the same day or on separate days. If you're well trained and chasing leg strength, keep the two more than two hours apart.

### Winter Cold by Metro: Average January Lows
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/winter-cold-by-metro/
NOAA's 1991–2020 average January low at weather stations in 48 big U.S. metros, and what cold, dark months change in a training week: the walk, not the lifting.
Short answer: NOAA's 1991–2020 normals put the average January low between 5.5 F (Minneapolis–St. Paul) and 61.0 F (Miami) at principal-city weather stations in 46 large U.S. metros, and 27 of the 46 average below freezing. In those months, move the daily walk indoors and keep the lifting plan exactly as it is.
Data (CSV): https://diogofit.com/learn/winter-cold-by-metro/winter-cold-by-metro.csv

### Bodyweight Workout at Home: A No-Equipment Plan
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/bodyweight-workout/
A no-equipment bodyweight workout for beginners at home: a squat, hinge, push, pull and core move, an easier and harder version of each, and how to progress.
Short answer: Train the whole body two or three times a week with five patterns: a squat, a hinge, a push, a pull and a core move. Use the version of each you can do for 8 to 20 good reps, stop each set with a few reps left, and move to a harder version once 20 gets easy.

### Commute Times and Working From Home by State
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/commute-by-state/
The Census Bureau's average trip to work and work-from-home share for all 50 states and DC, with margins of error, and where training fits around each.
Short answer: By the Census Bureau's 2020–2024 American Community Survey, the average trip to work runs from under 18 minutes (South Dakota and North Dakota) to 32.6 minutes (New York), and the share of workers who work from home from 5.9% (Mississippi) to 33.0% (District of Columbia). A long commute moves training before work, near work or into shorter sessions; working from home turns the old commute into a training slot.
Data (CSV): https://diogofit.com/learn/commute-by-state/commute-by-state.csv

### Hotel Workout: No Equipment or Hotel Gym (+ PDF)
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/hotel-workout/
A full-body hotel workout in two versions: the room with no equipment, or the hotel gym with dumbbells. Print the PDF and keep a travel week on track.
Short answer: A hotel workout needs a squat, a push, a pull and a hinge, plus a core move. In the room, use your bodyweight and take each set close to failure; in the hotel gym, add the dumbbells. Two short sessions hold a travel week together, and in one study, two weeks off barely moved squat or bench press strength.

### Average Annual Rainfall by Metro: NOAA Normals
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/rain-by-metro/
NOAA's 1991–2020 average annual precipitation at a named weather station in 40 U.S. metros, and what a wet day changes in a training week: the walk, not the lifting.
Short answer: NOAA's 1991–2020 normals put average annual precipitation between 7.2 inches (Phoenix) and 67.4 inches (Miami) at principal-city weather stations in 39 U.S. metros, and half of them get 41.8 inches or less. On a wet day, move the walk indoors or under cover and keep the lifting plan exactly as it is.
Data (CSV): https://diogofit.com/learn/rain-by-metro/rain-by-metro.csv

### How Many Sets per Week per Muscle?
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/how-many-sets-per-week/
How many sets per muscle per week: 6 to 10 hard sets is plenty when you're new, 10 or more builds more muscle, and returns shrink past about 20.
Short answer: Count the hard sets each muscle gets across the week. If you're new, 6 to 10 is plenty. The American College of Sports Medicine's 2026 review ties 10 or more to more muscle growth, with diminishing returns past about 18 to 20. Start where you can recover, and add a set or two when progress stalls.

### Commute Times and Working From Home by Metro
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/commute-by-metro/
The Census Bureau's average trip to work and work-from-home share for 40 U.S. metro areas, with margins of error, and where training fits around each.
Short answer: By the Census Bureau's 2020–2024 American Community Survey, the average trip to work across these 40 metro areas runs from 22.0 minutes (Grand Rapids) to 33.2 minutes (Riverside–San Bernardino), and the share of workers who work from home from 9.9% (Memphis) to 26.8% (Austin). A long commute moves training before work, near work or into shorter sessions; working from home turns the old commute into a training slot.
Data (CSV): https://diogofit.com/learn/commute-by-metro/commute-by-metro.csv

### How Many Reps to Build Muscle vs Strength?
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/how-many-reps/
How many reps per set: about 6 to 15 is the efficient middle for muscle, heavier sets of 1 to 6 build more strength, and there is no magic hypertrophy range.
Short answer: For muscle, a wide range of reps works when the sets are hard: about 6 to 15 is the efficient middle, and light sets of 15 to 40 work too when taken to failure. For strength, heavier sets of about 1 to 6 reps do more. There is no single hypertrophy range.

### How Active Is Your City? CDC Data for 27 Cities
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/how-active-is-your-city/
The CDC's PLACES estimates for 27 U.S. cities: adults with no leisure-time physical activity and adults reporting short sleep, with 95% ranges and how to read them.
Short answer: In the CDC's PLACES 2025 estimates (age-adjusted and model-based), the share of adults with no leisure-time physical activity runs from 13.0% (Centennial, Colorado) to 33.0% (San Bernardino, California) across these 27 cities, and the share who report short sleep, under seven hours, from 29.4% to 43.6%. Each end overlaps its neighbors, so no single city is clearly first or last.
Data (CSV): https://diogofit.com/learn/how-active-is-your-city/how-active-is-your-city.csv

### How Long to Rest Between Sets?
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/rest-between-sets/
How long to rest between sets: at least a minute for muscle growth, two to five for heavy compound lifts, less for small exercises, and how to time it.
Short answer: Rest at least a minute between sets for muscle growth: a 2024 meta-analysis found a small benefit past 60 seconds and no clear gain past 90. Give heavy compound lifts two to five minutes, smaller exercises one to two, and pair exercises for different muscles when time is short.

### Data Tables: Activity, Climate, Commute
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/data/
Eight CDC, NOAA and Census Bureau data tables for U.S. states, metros and cities: what each holds, its source and vintage, its CSV and how to cite it.
Short answer: This site has eight data tables built from public CDC, NOAA and Census Bureau data: physical activity by state, metro and city, summer heat, winter cold and rain by metro, and commute times by state and metro. Each has a CSV download and is free to reuse with credit to the agency and a link back.

### Supersets and Drop Sets, Explained
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/supersets/
What supersets and drop sets are, the three ways to pair exercises, what the research says about time and gains, and when to leave them out of your workout.
Short answer: A superset is two exercises done back to back, then a rest. In a 2025 meta-analysis, supersets kept about the same reps and total load as regular sets in a shorter session, with similar long-term gains in the few studies that tested them, though they felt harder. Pair different muscles, and keep heavy free-weight lifts out.

### Compound vs Isolation Exercises, Explained
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/compound-exercises/
What compound exercises are, the main movement patterns, how many to include, compound vs isolation exercises, and whether machines or free weights matter.
Short answer: Compound exercises move more than one joint and work several muscles at once, like squats, deadlifts, presses, rows and pulldowns. Build each session on at least a lower-body exercise, an upper-body push and an upper-body pull, do them early, and add isolation exercises for muscles you want more work for.

### How to Squat: Form, Depth and Common Faults
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/squat-form/
How to squat with good form: the setup step by step, how deep to go, whether your knees can pass your toes, the bar and dumbbell versions, and the faults.
Short answer: Feet about shoulder-width apart, toes turned out a little, brace, then sit down between your heels with your knees following your toes, as deep as you can hold that position, and stand back up. Depth matters: a 2021 meta-analysis found full range of motion built more strength and leg muscle than partial reps.

### How to Deadlift: Form, Trap Bar and RDL
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/deadlift-form/
How to deadlift with good form: learn the hip hinge first, then the conventional deadlift, the trap bar deadlift and the Romanian deadlift, and which to use.
Short answer: Learn the hip hinge first: push your hips back with your knees slightly bent and your back straight, then stand up by driving your hips forward. Then pick a version: the conventional deadlift from the floor, the trap bar, which often allows heavier loads, or the Romanian deadlift for the hamstrings.

### Bench Press Form, and How to Add Weight
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/bench-press-form/
Bench press form step by step: the setup, how wide to grip, whether to arch, the rep itself, and how to increase your bench press without rushing it.
Short answer: Lie with your eyes under the bar, feet flat and shoulder blades pulled back. Grip the bar wider than your shoulders: in two studies, medium and wide grips moved more weight than a shoulder-width or narrower one. Lower the bar under control to touch your chest, press it back up, and add weight in small steps.

### How to Do a Pull-Up, Even From Zero
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/how-to-do-a-pull-up/
How to do a pull-up with good form, and how to get your first one with negatives, bands, the assisted machine and the lat pulldown. Then how to add reps.
Short answer: Hang with straight arms, pull your shoulder blades down, and pull until your chin clears the bar, then lower all the way. If you can't do one yet, train the parts: slow negatives, band- or machine-assisted pull-ups and lat pulldowns. As each gets easier, take a little less help.

### Muscle Soreness (DOMS): How Long It Lasts
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/muscle-soreness/
What delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS) is, how long it usually lasts, whether to work out when you're sore, and when soreness is a reason to see a doctor.
Short answer: Delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS) usually appears 12 to 24 hours after exercise your muscles aren't used to, peaks one to three days after, and is gone within five to seven. You can usually still train: go lighter on the sore muscles for a day or two, or train others. Sharp pain or dark urine is different: see a doctor.

### Leg Day Workout: Gym and Dumbbell Versions
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/leg-day-workout/
A leg day workout for the gym and a dumbbell version: the exercises for quads, hamstrings, glutes and calves, the sets and reps, and how often to train legs.
Short answer: Cover four areas: a squat or leg press, a hinge such as the Romanian deadlift, a single-leg exercise like a lunge, then a seated leg curl and a standing calf raise. Don't count on squats for the hamstrings: in one nine-week trial, squats grew the thighs and glutes, but the hamstrings showed little to no growth.

### Back Workout: Pulldowns, Rows and a Hinge
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/back-workout/
Build a back workout from three slots: a vertical pull, a horizontal pull and a hinge. Pick one from each, for the gym, machines and cables, or home.
Short answer: Pick one exercise from each of three slots: a vertical pull (a pull-up or lat pulldown), a horizontal pull (a row) and a hinge (a Romanian deadlift or back extension). The 2026 ACSM position stand's authors suggest considering vertical and horizontal directions for the upper body, so do both. Three hard sets of each makes a session.

### Chest Workout: Press, Incline and Fly
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/chest-workout/
A chest workout built on a flat press, a low incline press and a fly, about ten hard sets a week, with a gym and a home version and the studies behind it.
Short answer: Build a chest workout on three exercises: a flat press, an incline press at about 30 degrees and a fly. Then count hard sets across the week: the American College of Sports Medicine's 2026 overview ties ten or more sets per muscle group a week to more muscle growth. At home, push-ups and dumbbells fill the same slots.

### Shoulder Workout: Front, Side and Rear Delts
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/shoulder-workout/
A shoulder workout for all three heads of the deltoid: the overhead press, lateral raises for the side, rows and reverse flies for the rear, gym or home.
Short answer: Train the three heads of the shoulder with three kinds of exercise: an overhead press for the front, lateral raises for the side, and rows, pull-ups or reverse flies for the rear. Pressing alone leaves the side short: in one ten-week bench press trial, the side of the shoulder lagged every other muscle measured.

### How to Do Push-Ups Correctly, Step by Step
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/how-to-do-push-ups/
How to do push-ups with good form, how to start on an incline when the floor is too hard, how many to do, and the harder versions once twenty get easy.
Short answer: Hands a little wider than your shoulders, body straight from head to heels: lower your chest close to the floor and press back up. Too hard from the floor? Put your hands on a counter or a bench, or drop to your knees; both take weight off your arms. Work lower over time, then raise your feet.

### Arm Workout: Curls, Triceps and Weekly Sets
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/arm-workout/
An arm workout that counts what presses and rows already give your biceps and triceps, then adds a curl and an overhead triceps extension. Gym or home.
Short answer: Count what your week already gives your arms. In a 2026 meta-regression, the counting method with the strongest evidence scored a set that trains a muscle only indirectly as half a set, so presses count toward your triceps and rows toward your biceps. Then add a curl and an overhead triceps extension after the compound lifts.

### Core Workout for Lifters: 4 Exercises
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/core-workout/
A core workout for people who lift: what squats and deadlifts already train, what they miss, and four exercises to add after your main lifts, gym or home.
Short answer: Heavy squats and deadlifts work the muscles along your spine harder than planks, side planks or ball exercises, but in the same studies they worked the abs and obliques no harder. So end your sessions with a short core block: a plank, a Pallof press, a carry and a crunch, two or three sets each.

### Cool-Down After a Workout: Do You Need One?
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/cool-down/
Do you need a cool-down after lifting? What studies of cool-downs and stretching after exercise found, what they didn't, and a short one if you like it.
Short answer: You don't need one. A 2018 review found an easy cool-down largely ineffective for next-day performance, soreness and most markers of recovery, and stretching after exercise hasn't cut soreness by a meaningful amount. If you like one, keep it short and easy: early evidence suggests it doesn't hold back what you gain from training.

### Mobility Routine for Lifters, in 10 Minutes
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/mobility-routine/
A ten-minute mobility routine for lifters (ankles, hips, upper back, shoulders), mobility vs flexibility in plain words, and what changes range over weeks.
Short answer: Flexibility is how far your soft tissues let a joint move, one trainable part of its range; mobility, as lifters use the word, is range you can reach and control in a lift. Lifting with weights improved range of motion about as much as stretching in a 2023 meta-analysis. For more range, add a ten-minute routine.

### Dumbbell vs Barbell, Lift by Lift
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/dumbbell-vs-barbell/
Dumbbell vs barbell for the bench, incline, shoulder press, row, RDL, curl and shrug: what the studies measured, what they found, and what they didn't test.
Short answer: A barbell usually lets you lift more weight; dumbbells let each side work on its own and make one-arm and one-leg versions easy. A 2025 meta-analysis found one-limb and two-limb training built similar muscle, while strength rose most in the version trained. So choose lift by lift, by what you most want to get strong at.

### Workout Log: What to Track and a Layout
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/workout-log/
What a workout log needs: exercise, weight, reps per set, reps in reserve and a note. A layout to copy on paper or in a notes app, and how to read it.
Short answer: A workout log needs five columns: the exercise, the weight, the reps in each set, how many reps you had left, and a short note. Before each session, read last week's line and beat it by a rep or a little weight. In a 2016 meta-analysis, monitoring progress helped more when it was physically recorded.

### How Much Weight Should I Lift?
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/how-much-weight-to-lift/
How much weight to lift: pick the reps first, then a weight that leaves two or three in reserve. Why charts miss, how beginners start, when to add weight.
Short answer: Choose the reps first, then a weight you can lift for that many with about two or three still in reserve. New lifters: guess lighter and leave three or four. When you can do one or two reps more than your target, add 2 to 10% to the weight.

### Hip Thrust: Form, Versions and Sets
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/hip-thrust/
How to do a hip thrust: bench, bar or dumbbell, foot position, the at-home and machine versions, hip thrust vs glute bridge, and how many sets to do.
Short answer: Sit with your upper back against a bench, the weight across your hips, feet flat about shoulder-width apart. Drive your hips up until your thighs are level with the floor and your shins are vertical, then lower under control. Do two or three hard sets of 8 to 12, after your squat or hinge.

### Goblet Squat: Form, Depth and When to Progress
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/goblet-squat/
How to do a goblet squat with a dumbbell or kettlebell: the setup, how deep to go, the bench or box version, the common faults, and when to move to a barbell.
Short answer: Hold one dumbbell or kettlebell against your chest, feet a little wider than your shoulders, toes turned out slightly. Sit down between your heels, elbows inside your knees, as deep as you can keep your heels down and your chest up, then stand. Full depth built more strength and leg muscle than partial reps in a 2021 meta-analysis.

### Dumbbell Row: Form, Versions, Muscles Worked
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/dumbbell-row/
How to do a dumbbell row: one-arm on a bench, standing, chest-supported and without a bench. The muscles it works, the common faults, and where it fits.
Short answer: One hand and one knee on a bench, back flat, dumbbell hanging under your shoulder. Pull your elbow back past your ribs, keeping it close to your side, then lower until your arm is straight. Two or three hard sets of 8 to 12 per arm. No bench? Brace your free hand on a chair or your thigh instead.

### Lat Pulldown Form: Grip, Cues and Faults
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/lat-pulldown-form/
Lat pulldown form: the setup, how wide to grip, the pull to your chest, leaning back and momentum, close-grip and standing versions, and the pull-up link.
Short answer: Thighs locked under the pad, hands one to two shoulder-widths apart, palms away. Pull the bar to the top of your chest, elbows driving down toward your back pockets, then let it rise until your arms are straight. Grip width changed lat activity little in a study of 15 men. Lean back slightly, no more.

### Leg Press: Foot Placement, Depth, vs Squat
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/leg-press/
How to use the leg press: setting the seat, where to put your feet and what it changes, how deep to go, the leg press vs the squat, and the common faults.
Short answer: Back and hips flat on the pad, feet about hip- to shoulder-width apart in the middle of the platform. Lower until your knees are bent to about a right angle or deeper, without your hips lifting off the seat, then press back up. Feet higher shifts some work to the glutes; lower, to the front of the thigh.

### Barbell Row Form: Grip, Bar Path, Pendlay
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/barbell-row-form/
Barbell row form step by step: the hinge angle, the bar path, overhand or underhand, where to put your hands, Pendlay vs bent-over, and the common faults.
Short answer: Hinge forward with soft knees until your torso is between about 45 degrees and parallel to the floor, back flat, bar hanging under your shoulders. Pull it in a straight line to your lower ribs or upper stomach, then lower it to straight arms, torso still the whole set. Two or three sets of 6 to 12.

### Free Workout Plans for the Gym or Home
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/workout-plans/
Free workout plans for the gym, dumbbells at home or no equipment, sorted by days a week. What a plan needs, which one fits your week, and the body-part days.
Short answer: A workout plan needs four things: the movements, the sets, reps and effort, a rule for progressing, and a shorter version for bad weeks. The free plans below all have them, sorted by days a week and equipment. Pick the one that fits the week you actually have, and log it.

### Training Glossary: Gym and Lifting Terms
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/glossary/
A training glossary in plain words: 98 gym and lifting terms, from reps in reserve and RPE to deloads, supersets, zone 2 and progressive overload, each linked.
Short answer: Three terms do most of the work in a training plan: reps in reserve (how many more good reps you could have done before failure), volume (the hard sets a muscle gets each week) and progressive overload (doing a little more than last time, on purpose). The other 95 are below, A to Z, each with a link.

### Romanian Deadlift: Form, Dumbbell, vs Deadlift
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/romanian-deadlift/
How to do a Romanian deadlift with a barbell, dumbbells or a kettlebell: how low to go, the muscles worked, how it differs from the deadlift, and the faults.
Short answer: Stand tall with the weight in front of your thighs, knees slightly bent. Push your hips back and let the weight slide down your legs until the backs of your thighs are fully stretched, usually around your knees to mid-shin. Drive your hips forward to stand up. Three sets of 8 to 12, with a barbell, dumbbells or a kettlebell.

### Overhead Press Form: Barbell, Dumbbell, Seated
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/overhead-press-form/
Overhead press form step by step with a barbell, dumbbells, seated or on a machine: grip, bar path, how to stop leaning back, and where it fits a shoulder day.
Short answer: Grip the bar just outside your shoulders, forearms upright, bar on the front of your shoulders. Brace your midsection and squeeze your glutes. Press straight up, moving your head back just enough for the bar to pass your face, then bring your head through so the bar finishes over it. Lower to your shoulders. Three sets of 6 to 12.

### Calf Workout: Gym, Dumbbells, At Home
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/calf-workout/
A calf workout for the gym, dumbbells or no equipment: standing vs seated raises and what each targets, range of motion, foot position, and sets and reps.
Short answer: Do standing calf raises with straight knees to train both calf muscles, and add seated raises for extra work on the deeper soleus. Lower all the way into a stretch, pause, then rise as high as you can. Three or four sets of 10 to 20, twice a week, on a machine, with a dumbbell, or on a step.

### How to Do a Plank Correctly, and How Long
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/how-to-do-a-plank/
How to do a plank correctly: setup and bracing cues, common faults, easier versions for beginners, harder ones, and what the research says about how long to hold.
Short answer: Forearms on the floor with your elbows under your shoulders, legs straight, up on your toes. Squeeze your glutes, brace your midsection and tuck your hips slightly so your body makes one straight line. Hold only as long as the line holds. When a hold in good position gets easy, move to a harder version rather than holding longer.

### Kettlebell Workout Plan: One Bell, Full Body
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/kettlebell-workout/
A full-body kettlebell workout plan for one bell: goblet squat, swing, press, row and carry, sets and reps, how to progress with one weight, and who it suits.
Short answer: Pick one kettlebell you can goblet squat for ten clean reps. Two or three days a week, do five movements: a goblet squat, a swing taught as a hip hinge, a one-arm press, a one-arm row and a carry. Two or three sets of each, stopping with two or three reps left, and add reps before you add weight.

### Resistance Band Workout Plan at Home
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/resistance-band-workout/
A full-body resistance band workout for home: the plan, legs, glutes and arms with a band, what bands do and don't do, and how to keep progressing with them.
Short answer: Two or three days a week, do six band movements: a squat, a hinge, a push, a row, a pulldown and a press, plus one core move. Do two or three sets of 12 to 20 reps, stopping one to three reps short of failure. Progress by adding reps, standing farther from the anchor, then moving to a thicker band.

### Cable Workout: A Full Session on One Station
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/cable-workout/
A full-body cable workout on one adjustable cable station: what cables do differently, the session, each body part, and when cables beat free weights.
Short answer: On one adjustable cable station, do eight exercises: a pull-through, a one-arm chest press, a kneeling one-arm pulldown, a row, a lateral raise, an overhead triceps extension, a curl and a Pallof press. Two or three sets of 10 to 15, stopping one or two reps short. Cables build muscle about as well as free weights.

### Forearm Workout and Grip for Lifters
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/forearm-workout/
A forearm workout for lifters: wrist curls, reverse curls, hammer curls, holds and carries, how much direct work you need after rows and deadlifts, and straps.
Short answer: Your rows, pulldowns and deadlifts already train your grip. Add two or three hard sets a week each of a wrist curl and a reverse or hammer curl, 12 to 20 reps, plus a heavy hold or carry. If your grip gives out before your back on heavy deadlifts, straps help those sets.

### Time Under Tension and Tempo: What It Does
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/time-under-tension/
What time under tension and lifting tempo mean, what the research shows for muscle growth and strength, eccentrics and negatives, and when to slow down.
Short answer: Time under tension is how long a set keeps a muscle working; tempo is the speed of each rep. In the trials, reps lasting from half a second to eight seconds built similar muscle when sets were taken to failure, and very slow reps looked worse. Lower under control, lift with intent, and judge sets by reps left.

### Glute Bridge: Form, Variations and Sets
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/glute-bridge/
How to do a glute bridge: where your feet go, the single-leg, march, hold and weighted versions, the machine, glute bridge vs hip thrust, and how many sets.
Short answer: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat, hip-width apart, close enough that your knees bend to about a right angle at the top. Push through your heels and raise your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to knees, pause, then lower. Do two or three hard sets of 8 to 20.

### Bulgarian Split Squat: Form, Stance and Sets
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/bulgarian-split-squat/
How to do a Bulgarian split squat: bench height, how far to step out, the dumbbell and bodyweight versions, the stance for glutes or thighs, and alternatives.
Short answer: Rest the top of your back foot on a knee-high bench, a long step in front of it. Lower straight down until your back knee nearly touches the floor, then drive up through your front foot. A longer step and a slight forward lean shift work to the hips. Do two or three sets of 8 to 12 a leg.

### Step-Ups: Form, Box Height, Muscles Worked
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/step-ups/
How to do step-ups: box height, pushing through the front foot, the dumbbell and knee-drive versions, muscles worked, and where step-ups fit a leg day.
Short answer: Put one whole foot on a box about knee height, lean forward slightly, and stand up by pushing through that front heel, letting the back foot just follow. Step down under control and repeat. Holding dumbbells at your sides, do two or three sets of 8 to 12 a leg, after your squat or hinge.

### Incline Bench Press: Angle, Form, Dumbbells
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/incline-bench-press/
Incline bench press with a barbell or dumbbells: the bench angle the studies favor for the upper chest, the setup, the faults, and incline vs flat.
Short answer: Set the bench to about 30 degrees, the angle where the upper chest was most active in a study of 30 trained adults. Shoulder blades back and down, feet flat, grip a little wider than your shoulders. Lower the bar or dumbbells to your upper chest, just below the collarbones, and press back up over your shoulders.

### Front Squat: Rack Position and vs Back Squat
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/front-squat/
How to front squat: the clean-grip, cross-arm and strap holds, the setup, depth, the faults, the dumbbell version, and the front squat vs the back squat.
Short answer: Rest the bar across the front of your shoulders, close to your throat, held with a clean grip, crossed arms or straps, elbows high. Feet about shoulder-width, brace, and sit straight down between your heels, torso upright, then stand. It trains the legs much like a back squat with a lighter bar: in one study, overall muscle activity was similar.

### Face Pulls: Cable Setup, Form and Versions
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/face-pulls/
How to do face pulls: the cable height and rope grip, the pull with elbows high, the turn at the end, common faults, band and dumbbell versions, and sets.
Short answer: Set a rope at about face height, step back until your arms are straight, and pull the rope toward your forehead with your elbows high. Finish with your hands beside your ears and your knuckles turned back. In a modeling study of 10 men, it loaded the rear shoulder about as much as a bent-over raise.

### Lateral Raises: Form, Cable vs Dumbbell, Machine
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/lateral-raises/
Lateral raise form with dumbbells, a cable or a machine: the arm path, the lean, what partial reps do, the swinging and shrugging faults, and sets and reps.
Short answer: Stand tall with light dumbbells at your sides. Raise your arms out to the sides, elbows nearly straight, until your hands reach shoulder height, then lower slowly. Keep the arm turned so your palms face the floor at the top. Dumbbells and cables grew the side of the shoulder about equally in 24 trained lifters.

### Leg Extension: Setup, Range, At-Home Options
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/leg-extension/
How to use the leg extension machine: seat and pad setup, how much range to use, why it reaches a muscle squats miss, at-home options, and common faults.
Short answer: Line your knees up with the machine's pivot and set the pad on your lower shins, just above the ankles. Straighten your legs until nearly locked, pause, then lower slowly to a deep knee bend. Don't skip the bottom half: in 45 untrained women, reps in the bent-knee half grew the thigh as well as or better than full reps.

### Leg Curl: Seated vs Lying, Form, At Home
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/leg-curl/
How to do the leg curl: seated vs lying and what the hamstring research found, the setup, tempo and foot position, at-home options, and common faults.
Short answer: Pick the seated leg curl if you have the choice. Knees lined up with the pivot, pad just above the heels, thigh pad snug. Curl your heels down and back as far as they go, then return slowly to nearly straight. In 20 young adults, the seated version grew the hamstrings more than the lying one, 14% against 9%.

### Hack Squat: Foot Placement, Depth, vs Leg Press
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/hack-squat/
How to use the hack squat machine: the setup, where to put your feet, how deep to go, the hack squat vs the leg press and the squat, and the common faults.
Short answer: Back flat on the pad, shoulders under the pads, feet about shoulder-width in the middle of the platform. Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the platform, then press up through your whole foot. In 10 men, the hack squat allowed a heavier max than the back squat but asked less of most of the trunk muscles.

### Seated Cable Row: Form, Grip and Faults
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/seated-cable-row/
Seated cable row form: the setup, the pull to your stomach, neutral vs wide grip, leaning and momentum, single-arm and machine versions, and alternatives.
Short answer: Feet on the platform, knees slightly bent, sit tall. Pull the handle to your stomach with your elbows close, then let your arms go long without rounding forward. A 2026 review linked a narrower grip and elbows kept closer to the body with more lat activity. Keep your torso nearly still: lean back a little, no more.

### Chest Fly: Dumbbell, Cable and Machine Form
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/chest-fly/
How to do a chest fly with dumbbells, cables or a machine: the arc, the stretch, fly vs bench press in the research, common faults, and how many sets.
Short answer: Arms out wide with a slight, fixed bend at the elbow, bring your hands together in a wide arc in front of your chest, then open until you feel a stretch, no deeper. Keep it after your presses. A fly machine alone grew the chest in 15 untrained men over 12 weeks.

### Hamstring Workout: Gym, Home, No Equipment
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/hamstring-workout/
A hamstring workout for the gym and for home with dumbbells, bands or no equipment: why you need a hinge and a curl, seated vs lying curls, sets and reps.
Short answer: Train both jobs of the hamstrings: a hinge such as the Romanian deadlift, which extends the hip, and a curl, which bends the knee. In 42 young men, a hip-bent curl and the Nordic curl grew different hamstring muscles most. Three sets of each, once or twice a week; at home, single-leg hinges, slider curls and Nordic curls.

### Ankle Mobility: Knee-to-Wall Test, Drills
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/ankle-mobility/
Ankle mobility for lifters: why ankle range matters in the squat, the knee-to-wall test, calf stretches and drills, raised heels, and what the evidence shows.
Short answer: Test it first: foot a few inches from a wall, push your knee toward the wall with your heel down, and measure the farthest spot that still works. In 20 healthy adults, that range was the only measure linked with how deep they squatted. Calf stretching adds a few degrees; raised heels are the quick workaround.

### Zone 2 Cardio: Heart Rate and the Talk Test
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/zone-2-cardio/
What zone 2 cardio is (heart rate, the talk test, lactate), how to find your zone 2 without a lab, how much a week beside lifting, and examples to start with.
Short answer: Zone 2 is steady cardio just below your first threshold, the point where your breathing starts to pick up: an expert panel put it immediately below the first lactate or ventilatory threshold. Without a lab, you can still talk in full sentences, but it isn't effortless. Beside lifting, aim for the WHO's 150 to 300 moderate minutes weekly.

### Hammer Curls: Form, Muscles Worked, vs Curls
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/hammer-curls/
How to do hammer curls: what the thumbs-up grip shifts to the brachialis and brachioradialis, hammer vs regular curls, and the cable and rope versions.
Short answer: Hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your thighs, and curl with your thumbs up, elbows still at your sides. The grip shifts less than its reputation: in 10 competitive bodybuilders, the palms-up curl worked the biceps and the brachioradialis slightly harder. Use it as a second curl: two or three hard sets of 8 to 15.

### Bodyweight Squat: Form, Progression and Sets
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/bodyweight-squat/
How to do a bodyweight squat: the form, squatting to a bench, tempo and pauses, what bodyweight squats build and what they don't, and what comes next.
Short answer: Feet about shoulder-width apart, toes turned out a little, arms forward for balance. Sit down between your heels as deep as you can keep them on the floor, then stand. Start to a bench and lower it in steps. Sets of 8 to 20; once 20 is easy, slow the lowering, pause at the bottom, or add a weight.

### Sled Push: Form, Muscles and Alternatives
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/sled-push/
How to do a sled push: the load, handle height and stride, what it trains, sled pushes vs pulls, how to fit it beside lifting, and alternatives without a sled.
Short answer: Load the sled so you can keep it moving without stopping. Hold the handles with your arms long, lean in until you're in a straight line from head to back foot, and drive with short, quick steps for 10 to 20 meters. Rest until you can push hard again, four to six times, after lifting or on another day.

### Good Mornings: Form, Versions and vs RDL
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/good-mornings/
How to do the good morning exercise: the setup, where the bar sits, how far to bend, the faults, dumbbell and band versions, and good mornings vs the RDL.
Short answer: Set the bar across your upper back, slightly higher than for a squat, feet about shoulder-width apart, knees soft. Push your hips back and bow forward until your torso nears parallel or the backs of your thighs are fully stretched, then drive your hips forward to stand. Start light: two or three sets of 8 to 12.

### Hip Mobility for Lifters: Checks and Drills
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/hip-mobility/
Hip mobility for lifting: the hip range a squat and a hinge use, simple checks, 90/90, hip flexor and adductor drills, and what the evidence shows.
Short answer: Check the two positions your lifts use: the bottom of a bodyweight squat with your heels down, and a hinge with your back flat. If one falls short, add a few drills after lifting, and lift through your full range: in 25 untrained adults, full-range lifting improved hip range about as much as stretching did.

### Glute Workout: Gym, Home and Band Versions
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/glute-workout/
A glute workout for the gym and for home with dumbbells or bands: the exercises, the sets and reps, how often to train glutes, and what the research shows.
Short answer: Cover three jobs: a hip thrust or glute bridge, a hinge such as the Romanian deadlift, and a single-leg exercise like the Bulgarian split squat or a step-up. Do two or three hard sets of each, once or twice a week, and count your squats and lunges toward ten or more glute sets a week.

### Strength Training for Women: A Weekly Plan
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/strength-training-for-women/
Strength training for women: how to set up the week, how heavy to lift and how many reps, how to progress, rest, and what the studies in women found.
Short answer: Train each major muscle at least twice a week, in sets of about 6 to 15 taken close to failure, and add a little over time. In women, a 24-study meta-analysis found large strength gains and medium muscle growth.

### Strength Training Over 40: What Changes
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/strength-training-over-40/
Strength training over 40 and 50: what research shows about strength and muscle later in life, how heavy to lift, warm-ups, recovery, days a week and a plan.
Short answer: Strength and muscle respond to lifting well past 40. In 47 studies of 1,079 adults aged 50 and over, strength rose on each of the four tests analysed. What changes is the pacing, as practice rather than research: a full warm-up, smaller jumps, planned recovery.

### Unilateral Exercises: Benefits and Examples
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/unilateral-exercises/
Unilateral exercises train one arm or leg at a time: what they do for muscle and strength, the bilateral deficit, imbalances, examples and how to program them.
Short answer: Unilateral exercises train one arm or leg at a time: split squats, step-ups, single-leg Romanian deadlifts, one-arm rows and presses. In a 2025 review of nine studies, they showed no significant difference in muscle growth from two-limb lifts, and strength rose most in whichever version was trained. Add one or two after your main lift, weaker side first.

### How to Do Lunges: Form, Versions, Dumbbells
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/how-to-do-lunges/
How to do lunges properly: the forward, reverse and walking lunge, lunges with dumbbells and at home, what they train, the common mistakes and how to progress.
Short answer: Take a long step forward and lower until both knees are bent about 90 degrees, front heel down and back knee just above the floor, then push through the front foot to stand back up. Start with bodyweight reverse lunges, two or three sets of 8 to 12 a leg, then hold dumbbells at your sides.

### How to Do Dips: Chest vs Triceps, at Home
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/how-to-do-dips/
How to do dips properly: parallel-bar dips for chest or triceps, bench and chair dips at home without a dip bar, band-assisted dips and negatives, and mistakes.
Short answer: Hold parallel bars with straight arms, lower until your upper arms are about level with the floor, then press up. Coaches usually say to lean forward with elbows slightly out for more chest and stay upright with elbows close for more triceps, though no study has measured it. No bars? Start with bench dips, then assisted dips and negatives.

### Mind-Muscle Connection: Meaning and Evidence
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/mind-muscle-connection/
What the mind-muscle connection means, what the trials show for muscle activity, growth and strength, when it helps and when it doesn't, and how to practise it.
Short answer: The mind-muscle connection means focusing on the muscle you're training rather than on moving the weight. At light and moderate loads it raises that muscle's activity, and in one eight-week trial in untrained men it grew the elbow flexors (the biceps and its neighbours) more. For a single all-out effort, focusing on the movement works better.

### Online Coach vs Fitness App vs AI Trainer
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/online-coach-vs-fitness-app-vs-ai/
Online coach, fitness app or AI chatbot? What each one gives you, what it costs in time and money, who it suits and where it falls short.
Short answer: A fitness app gives you a plan, a place to log it and reminders. An AI chatbot writes a draft plan from whatever you tell it. An online coach writes the plan around your week, reads your numbers and changes it with you. Pick by what's missing: a plan, or someone who notices when you stop.

### Rear Delt Fly: Dumbbell, Cable and Machine
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/rear-delt-fly/
How to do a rear delt fly with dumbbells, cables or the reverse pec deck: the arm path, palms in or down, what it trains in the studies, faults and sets.
Short answer: Hinge forward with dumbbells, or sit facing a reverse pec deck, elbows slightly bent. Sweep your arms out and back until they line up with your body, then lower slowly. In 12 men with strength-training experience, the machine produced more rear-delt activity than a seated row or an inclined lat pulldown. Two or three sets of 12 to 16.

### Tricep Pushdown: Form, Rope vs Bar, Sets
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/tricep-pushdown/
How to do a tricep pushdown: rope or bar, where your elbows go, what it does for the long head next to an overhead extension, strict reps, faults and sets.
Short answer: Clip a rope or bar to a high cable, pin your elbows to your sides, and press down until your arms are straight, then let your forearms rise to a right angle. In 21 adults over 12 weeks, that arm-at-the-side position grew the long head 19.6%, and the same extension overhead grew it 28.5%.

### Preacher Curl: Form, Setup, vs Incline Curl
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/preacher-curl/
How to do a preacher curl: setting the pad, how far to lower, what the trials found against the incline curl, the bar, dumbbell and cable versions, and sets.
Short answer: Sit so your armpits rest on the top edge of the pad and the backs of your upper arms lie flat on it. Curl up, then lower until your arms are almost straight. In 21 untrained adults over 12 weeks, total elbow-flexor growth didn't differ significantly between preacher and incline curls: 19.2% and 17.6%.

### Chest Press Machine: Setup, Form, vs Bench
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/chest-press-machine/
How to use the chest press machine: seat height and handle position, the press, machine vs bench press in the studies, when a beginner starts here, and faults.
Short answer: Set the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest, keep your back against the pad, and press until your arms are straight, then return the handles to chest level under control. A 2023 meta-analysis found no significant difference in muscle growth between free-weight and machine training in the five studies that measured it.

### Sumo Squat: Form, Muscles Worked, Versions
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/sumo-squat/
How to do a sumo squat: stance width and toe angle, the dumbbell, kettlebell and barbell versions, what a wide stance changes for the glutes and inner thighs.
Short answer: Stand with your feet well outside your shoulders and your toes turned out, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell between your legs. Sit straight down between your heels, knees following your toes, then stand. In nine male lifters, stance width changed inner-thigh and glute activity but didn't isolate any part of the quadriceps.

### Arnold Press: Form, Muscles Worked, Mistakes
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/arnold-press/
How to do the Arnold press: the palms-in start, the turn, seated or standing, what a shoulder press trains, what is untested, the common faults and the sets.
Short answer: Sit tall, dumbbells in front of your shoulders, palms facing you. Press up while turning your palms forward to straight arms, and reverse the turn on the way down. No study has tested the Arnold press itself; in 13 men experienced in strength training, a seated barbell shoulder press produced the highest front-shoulder muscle activity of four exercises tested.

### Upright Row: Form, Grip, Muscles Worked
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/upright-row/
How to do an upright row: grip width, how high to pull, what it trains in the shoulders and traps, the barbell, dumbbell and cable versions, and the sets.
Short answer: Stand tall holding a bar or dumbbells in front of your thighs, hands about shoulder width or wider. Pull straight up your body, elbows leading, until your elbows reach about shoulder height, then lower. In 16 weight-trained men, the widest grip tested produced more shoulder and trapezius activity and less biceps activity.

### Box Squat: Form, Height, vs Regular Squat
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/box-squat/
How to do a box squat: setting the box height, touch-and-go or sit and pause, what the studies found it changes against a regular squat, faults and sets.
Short answer: Set a box or bench behind you at the depth you want, usually thighs about parallel to the floor. Squat back and down to it, pause without relaxing, then stand. In eight resistance-trained men doing single reps, a box squat and a regular squat showed similar peak force and power, and muscle activity was generally higher in the regular squat.

### Zercher Squat: Form, Setup, vs Front Squat
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/zercher-squat/
How to do a Zercher squat: the rack height, the hold, keeping the arms comfortable, what a front-loaded squat changes, how it compares, and the sets.
Short answer: Set the bar in a rack at about the height of your lower ribs, cradle it in the crooks of your elbows with your hands together, and squat straight down with your torso upright. No study has tested the Zercher squat itself; in 26 healthy men, a front squat produced more trunk muscle activity than a back squat.

### Back Extension: Form, Muscles, Versions
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/back-extension/
How to do a back extension on a 45-degree bench: the hip hinge, the glute version, hand and knee positions, the reverse hyper, what training does, and sets.
Short answer: Set the pad just below your hip bones, hook your heels, and hinge forward from the hips, back held still. Rise until your body forms one line, then lower. Told to hinge at the hips, spine held still, 16 adults with strength-training experience had larger turning forces at the back and hips than when told to curl the spine.

### Dumbbell Pullover: Form, Chest or Lats?
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/dumbbell-pullover/
How to do a dumbbell pullover on a bench or the floor, whether it trains the chest or the lats, straight vs bent arms, the faults, and the sets.
Short answer: Lie on a bench holding one dumbbell over your chest, elbows slightly bent. Lower it back behind your head in an arc until your upper arms are about level with your ears, then pull it back over your chest. In 8 healthy men, a barbell pullover worked the chest more than the lats.

### Group Fitness Classes vs Personal Training
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/group-fitness-vs-personal-training/
Group fitness classes vs personal training or 1-on-1 coaching: who writes the plan, attention per person, accountability, cost in words, who each suits.
Short answer: A group fitness class gives you a set time, an instructor at the front and other people in the room, with one workout for everyone. One-to-one coaching gives you a plan written for you and a person who reads your numbers and changes it. Pick a class if showing up is the hard part and you like training with others. Pick a coach if the plan has to be written for you, or you stop when nobody is watching your week.

### Gym Membership vs Personal Trainer or Coach
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/gym-membership-vs-personal-trainer/
Gym membership vs a personal trainer or online coach: what a membership alone gives you, how often new members stop going, what each adds, who needs which.
Short answer: A gym membership gives you the equipment and the door. It doesn't bring a plan, or anyone who notices when you stop going. A trainer at the gym adds live coaching in the session; an online coach adds a plan for the whole week and someone reading your numbers. If you know what to do and you go, the membership alone is enough. If your last membership went unused by month three, what's missing is a plan and a person, not a better gym.

### Straight-Arm Pulldown: Form and Muscles
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/straight-arm-pulldown/
How to do a straight-arm pulldown at a cable: the setup, bar or rope, what it trains, how it differs from the lat pulldown and pullover, faults and sets.
Short answer: Stand facing a high cable, hold a bar or rope at about head height with arms long and elbows slightly bent, and sweep it down in an arc to your thighs, then let it rise. PubMed lists no study of it by name; in 17 men, held shoulder extension, its movement, produced the most lat activity of four.

### Landmine Press: Form, Muscles and Setup
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/landmine-press/
How to do a landmine press: the anchor, standing or kneeling, one arm or two, what the angle means for chest and shoulders, the faults, and the sets.
Short answer: Wedge one end of a barbell into a corner or an anchor, hold the other end at your shoulder, and press it up and forward until your arm is straight, then lower it. PubMed lists no study of its muscle activity; in a bench-angle study, the more upright the press, the more the front of the shoulder worked.

### Are YouTube Workouts Effective? Videos vs a Coach
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/youtube-workouts-vs-coaching/
Are YouTube workouts effective? What a trial of free workout videos found, where free videos and programs stop, what a coach adds, and how to decide.
Short answer: Yes, YouTube workouts can be effective: in a 12-week trial, young adults sent weekly workout videos did more moderate-to-vigorous activity and more strength work than a group sent health-education videos. What free videos don't do is write the plan around your week, progress it, or notice when you stop. If you follow a video and keep following it, you don't need a coach. If you've saved twenty videos and done four, the videos aren't the problem.

### Pistol Squat: Form, Progression, Muscles
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/pistol-squat/
How to do a pistol squat: the steps, five progressions from a box to the full rep, what it trains, why ankle range matters, the faults, and the sets.
Short answer: Stand on one leg, the other held straight out in front, and squat down as low as you can with your heel flat, then stand back up. Build to it with box and assisted versions. PubMed lists no study of it by name; in 11 lifters, a loaded single-leg squat worked the side glute hardest of three.

### Trap Workout: Shrugs, Rows, Raises, Sets
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/trap-workout/
A trap workout for the upper, middle and lower traps: dumbbell and barbell shrugs, rows, raises and the deadlift, what the studies measured, and the sets.
Short answer: Train the upper traps with shrugs, dumbbells at your sides or a barbell in front, lifting your shoulders straight up toward your ears. Add a row and a raise for the middle and lower traps. In 30 healthy people, a one-arm shrug produced the most upper-trap activity of ten exercises.
